findings.evidence: `Module.Projective.of_split` is in the `Semiring` section of Mathlib (`mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Projective.lean:164`, section opened at `:76`, closed `:209`, variables `[Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid P]`); `LinearMap.mulRight` needs only `[Semiring R] [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring A] [IsScalarTower R A A]` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Defs.lean:1008,1035,1043`); `Ideal.mem_span_singleton'` is in `section Semiring` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Span.lean:40,93`); `LinearMap.codRestrict` is semilinear/semiring-level (`Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/LinearMap.lean:157`).
findings.fix: State `theorem projective_span_singleton {A : Type*} [Semiring A] {e : A} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) : Module.Projective A (Ideal.span {e} : Ideal A)`; the proof body should go through unchanged.
findings.issue: `IsIdempotentElem.projective_span_singleton` assumes `[Ring A]`, but nothing in the proof needs subtraction; the rest of the `Ae` API in this repo is deliberately semiring-level (see the implementation note in `Idempotents/Primitive/Basic.lean:56`, "the API for the left ideal `Ae` are stated over a semiring").

findings.evidence: `Ideal.isNilpotent_of_mem_ker_endMapQ` has no projectivity hypothesis (`TauCeti/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/EndQuotient.lean:119`), whereas `Ideal.endMapQ_surjective` requires `[Module.Projective R M]` (`:76`) and is used only at `Top.lean:102` in the `mpr` branch; `isIndecomposableModule_iff_nontrivial_and_forall_isIdempotentElem` is projectivity-free (`TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullSchmidt/Indecomposable.lean:160`), and `IsSimpleModule.isIndecomposableModule` (`:167`) needs no hypotheses either.
findings.fix: Extract the reflecting direction without the instance, e.g. `omit [Module.Projective R P] in theorem IsIndecomposableModule.of_quotient_smul_top (hI : IsNilpotent I) (h : IsIndecomposableModule R (P ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R P))) : IsIndecomposableModule R P`, prove the iff from it, and likewise expose `IsIndecomposableModule.of_isSimpleModule_quotient_jacobson_smul_top` (semiprimary, no projectivity) with the iff at line 108 derived from both halves.
findings.issue: `isIndecomposableModule_quotient_smul_top_iff` inherits `[Module.Projective R P]` from the section variables, but the `mp` direction (`P ⧸ I • ⊤` indecomposable → `P` indecomposable, lines 91–97) uses only the nil kernel and `Submodule.mkQ_surjective`; projectivity enters solely in the `mpr` branch. The same under-generalization recurs at line 108: the `mpr` of `isIndecomposableModule_iff_isSimpleModule_quotient_jacobson_smul_top` (top simple → `P` indecomposable) factors through that projectivity-free direction. As stated, the standard fact "a module with indecomposable/simple top over a ring with nilpotent radical is indecomposable" is unavailable for non-projective modules.

summary: Two statements carry hypotheses stronger than their proofs need: `projective_span_singleton` asks for a ring where a semiring suffices, and the indecomposability-from-the-top direction is locked behind a `Module.Projective` instance it never uses.
